In 3rd grade I was diagnosed with ADD by a psychologist. I had not asked my parents for a psychologist meeting because of an inability to concentrate or sit still. I had instead raised concerns about self destructive and suicidal urges. 3 meetings later, I left with a prescription for stimulants for the ADD that this doctor had definitely discovered. My initial issue was never addressed, though the Concerta I was now on DID help keep them in check slightly, though not by enough to eliminate my fears of one day carrying them out. In the years since, I have consulted a friend who is a nationally recognized forensic psychiatrist, and she stated that, in the many years she has known me, she has not seen any significant behavior or evidence that my unmedicated behavior is abnormal, or was when I was a child, save for a computerized test I took to confirm the first doctor's suspicion before he made the final diagnosis (I'm afraid I have been unable to find the name for this test, it consisted of a black rectangle with a white box inside it at either the top or bottom that would flash onscreen for a very short moment, I was supposed to press a button whenever the square was at the top of the box, but not the bottom). This test is not conclusive in diagnosing ADD/ADHD (no test is considered conclusive). My older sister was in school for psychology at the time this diagnosis was made, and we have, of course, talked about it since, She now has her degree and has told me that she ALSO disagrees with the diagnosis of ADD, stating that the behavior and thoughts I describe is most similar to certain types of OCD.

If you read through that wall of text, you should be seeing a problem here, I went to a doctor for one set of symptoms, was given a diagnosis and medication addressing a different set of symptoms I had never complained about. Other psychiatric professionals who have interacted with me far more extensively than Doc number 1 have both disagreed with the initial conclusion. My initial set of symptoms have never been resolved save by improving my self control and mental discipline on my own. Despite this, I continue to take the provided medication because it DOES help me remain productive, but I know from experience I don't actually need it so long as I care about what i'm doing or find it interesting.

TL;DR: Diagnostics for ADD/ADHD and other similar disorders are incredibly lacking, nor is their much effort to rectify this issue.
